question: According to arXiv:1411.4647v2, annihilation into pairs of on-shell Higgs bosons can fit the Fermi GeV excess. Under which condition is the fit good, and what are the best-fit dark matter mass, annihilation cross section, χ² and p-value for this channel? How does the paper explain that the fit is good although its best-fit dark matter mass is more than twice that of the b b̄ channel?

arguments.answer:
The paper says the hh channel gives a rather good fit "so long as h is produced close to rest" (on-shell Higgs pairs, with m_χ just above m_h). For pure hh annihilation (Tab. 1) the best fit is m_χ ≈ 125.7 (+3.1/−0) GeV and ⟨σv⟩ ≈ 5.33 ± 0.68 ×10⁻²⁶ cm³/s. This has χ²_min = 29.5 and p-value = 0.13. The b b̄ best fit is m_χ ≈ 48.7 GeV, so the hh mass is more than twice as large.

The paper explains the good fit as a cascade effect. hh can be treated like cascade annihilation through intermediate states. Each h decays mainly to b b̄, and each b quark then has energy ≈ m_h/2. The b quarks are therefore boosted, and the resulting spectrum resembles b b̄ from a lighter DM particle. That is why the fit is good even though the DM mass is over twice as heavy as for the other channels.
